title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator joins channel meetings
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and rollout schedule match Microsoft's records, and its existing governance controls and licensing statements are supported. It distinguishes the planned channel-meeting capability from general Facilitator documentation and explicitly flags the inconsistent PowerShell blocking examples.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: row 1; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Teams admin center route to allow or block Facilitator is Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
select Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select Facilitator from the app list.
In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $false is documented as unblocking an app; Id takes the Teams app application ID.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 2b876f4d-2e6b-4ee7-9b09-8893808c1380 -IsBlocked $false
Unblocks 1Page App
Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.

claims.claim: The same reference also describes an example using IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app

claims.claim: The reference does not state a reliable blocking value because its true and false examples both say unblocking.
claims.quote: Searched: Update-M365TeamsApp IsBlocked true block app. Read the complete update-m365teamsapp reference and search excerpts; examples 2 and 3 describe true as unblocking, example 4 describes false as unblocking, and the parameter description supplies no resolution.

claims.quote:

You can then assign the policy to your entire tenant or to a select group of users.

claims.claim: Facilitator is allowed by default unless all apps are blocked for the organisation.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: row 2; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled $false disables collaborative AI-generated meeting notes.
claims.quote:
Collaborative meeting notes | IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled (boolean)
Disable Loop workspace creation and Loop component creation and integration everywhere
Set-SPOTenant -IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled $false

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI for the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled property is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled admin center UI setting collaborative AI meeting notes. Read facilitator-teams and Loop components configuration; the property uses PowerShell, while the documented admin-centre checkbox controls Loop workspace creation.

claims.where: controls[1].scope and note; Governance controls: row 2
claims.claim: The collaborative meeting notes property applies tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level. This means that if you disable this setting, AI-generated notes for meetings is turned off for all users in your organization.

claims.claim: The SharePoint property does not apply to collaborative meeting notes in Teams New Calendar, where Cloud Policy applies instead.
claims.quote: The SharePoint organization property doesn't apply to collaborative meeting notes in Teams New Calendar, see Settings management in Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: Managing Loop experiences in Teams requires the SharePoint PowerShell module.
claims.quote: You'll need the latest version of SharePoint PowerShell module to enable or disable Loop experiences in Teams.

claims.claim: The channel meeting scheduling control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting scheduling > Channel meeting scheduling.
claims.quote:
expand Meetings > Meeting policies and choose the policy you want to update.
Under Meeting scheduling
To restrict who can schedule meetings in a channel, toggle Channel meeting scheduling to Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False prevents users assigned that policy from scheduling new channel meetings.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False

claims.claim: Channel meeting scheduling is an existing per-user meeting scheduling policy rather than a Facilitator-specific control.
claims.quote:
These settings are per-user policies and they apply before a meeting starts.
Channel meeting scheduling: Controls whether a user can schedule a meeting in a channel.

claims.claim: With channel meeting scheduling off, the organiser can still edit existing channel meetings.
claims.quote: If this setting is turned off, users can't create new channel meetings, but the event organizer can edit existing channel meetings.

claims.claim: Turning off meeting policy settings disables join links for existing meetings of that type that the affected user organised.
claims.quote: The meeting join links and conference IDs of all existing meetings of that type that the user previously started or scheduled don't work.

claims.claim: Turning off meeting policy settings disables conference IDs for existing meetings of that type that the affected user organised.
claims.quote: The meeting join links and conference IDs of all existing meetings of that type that the user previously started or scheduled don't work.

claims.claim: Existing meeting content remains accessible after meeting policy settings are turned off.
claims.quote: The conversations, files, whiteboards, recordings, transcripts, and other content related to the meeting are retained and users can still access them.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting that restricts Facilitator to or from channel meetings only.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator channel meeting only restrict block Teams meeting policy PowerShell. Read facilitator-teams and manage-who-can-schedule-meetings; controls govern general app availability or channel scheduling, not channel-only Facilitator use.

claims.claim: Purview says to use a retention policy with the Teams chats option for Facilitator AI interactions in meetings.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.

claims.claim: Purview says to use a retention policy with the OneDrive accounts option for Facilitator AI-generated meeting notes.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI-generated notes in meetings, use a retention policy or retention labels with the OneDrive accounts option.

claims.claim: Facilitator meeting notes are visible to meeting participants.
claims.quote: Collaborative, real-time notes editable by all participants via the Notes tab

claims.claim: The collaborative meeting notes property cannot be configured per user.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.where: Governance controls: row 2; Governance guidance: After rollout
